src/loader/executable_image.cpp.reason: PE mapping/import/export/rebase infrastructure for reference guest execution and source facts; no recovered game policy inside this module.
src/loader/executable_image.cpp.semantic_justification: Complete header and implementation reviewed: bounded little-endian file reads, MZ/PE32/i386 identification, header/section mapping and zero tails, named exports/forwarders, RVA-to-VA conversion, HIGHLOW rebasing, import descriptors/thunks/name-or-ordinal and u32 reads. VAs mean guest image locations by their use, not their magnitude. MZ/PE signatures, machine/magic, ordinal flag, relocation type/offset masks and field offsets are legitimate format encodings. Missing image bytes/export names and malformed image results are real boundary absence, not gameplay fixture fields. No game-mode, allocation policy or resource-selection algorithm is recovered here. Caller-owned PE reads can still feed legacy fixture optionals; this API does not make those callers conforming. Code is densely packed and rebased has an unchecked optional dereference, so purpose does not establish code conformity.

resolved_owners.resolution: ExecutableImage owns bytes, sections, exports and directory metadata as a value. HleModules stores shared mapped images per GuestModule; X86Guest copies their bytes into separate mutable guest execution memory. NativeGameConfiguration holds shared const input/game/model images; writes before/within the guest are not modeled as image mutations.

resolved_consumers.resolution: HleModules parses/rebases DLLs, maps them and resolves named exports; bind_imports writes resolved targets to IAT VAs in X86Guest. App/reference session parses the main image. override_table reads source image facts. ModelDllSet maps DLL exports/action pointers through this API and remains an address-bearing game-directory consumer needing its own migration; no exemption is conferred on it.

accepted_judges.accepted_scope: Existing guest_imports assertions cover pinned 9-DLL/159-import parsing, ordinal import, exact IAT slots and HLE trap binding. model_dlls covers exact export case, rebased exports/HIGHLOW data, distinct mapping and missing slot. guest_dlls exercises real module loading and profile writes.
accepted_judges.limits: Historical accepted paths only, not rerun. No exhaustive malformed/truncated image, relocation-size, ordinal export, forwarder-chain or Windows loader equivalence qualification is established. Source-backed P2 is not excluded by these tests.

findings.title: Reject relocation entries outside mapped image before dereferencing
findings.description: rebased validates block size against the declared relocation directory extent, but not against mapped.size(). The entry loop unconditionally dereferences le(mapped,e,2). Static example: SizeOfImage 4096, relocation RVA 4088 and directory size 10, readable final 8-byte block header declaring block size 10. Both header reads succeed and block passes validation; first entry starts at byte 4096, le returns nullopt and operator* violates its precondition. parse accepts the directory metadata without checking mapped extent. This is an actual unchecked boundary in a malformed-image path, not an address-style violation or an observed supported-image failure.
findings.suggested_followup: In a separate source/judge packet, bounds-check directory/block entries and retain explicit error results; add discriminating malformed-image coverage without weakening pinned-image checks.
findings.validation: Static complete-body reasoning only; no input constructed or executed.

src/loader/guest_heap.cpp.reason: Synthetic byte/identity/availability backing for reference-composed legacy heap callers; recovered allocator wrappers and game policies are separate consumers.
src/loader/guest_heap.cpp.semantic_justification: Complete header and implementation reviewed: constructor parameters define synthetic guest token/address space; create traces one token, alloc validates handle and 32-bit capacity, rounds zero-size storage to one byte and spans to eight bytes plus a gap, free erases only exact bases, upper_bound resolves reads/writes within owned blocks. The allocation map, byte availability and trace are per-instance, with no original GLOBAL owner. Default token/base are deliberate reference identities, not recovered Windows allocation observations. 32-bit maximum and alignment masks are numeric encodings. alloc nullopt represents modeled failure; read nullopt deliberately combines unmapped storage and indeterminate unwritten bytes. This unknown byte model is appropriate reference infrastructure and must not be carried into native gameplay state. Lazy heap creation/global publication and CD/system allocation policies remain in engine/game callers, not hidden inside this module.

resolved_owners.resolution: NativeGame reference composition owns heap_ and separate crt_heap_ identities; NinjaMemoryState separately owns the source heap handle word. Borrowed NinjaSystemInitRuntime carries heap references. GuestHeap does not own that source global and is not a second owner of it. Real x86 HLE HeapCreate/HeapAlloc use HleProcess handles plus HleMemory, not this backing map.

resolved_consumers.resolution: nj_malloc/nj_free overloads adapt the synthetic heap into NinjaMemoryMethods, converting allocation nullopt to completed DWORD zero; host-unavailable optional and ordinary failure remain distinct. run_cd_drive_scan writes/reads drive-list bytes through this heap; system init borrows it for pools/buffers. Their source-address state/dispatch/fixture concerns are real recovered caller behavior outside these six files, not justified infrastructure by association.

accepted_judges.accepted_scope: guest_heap assertions cover synthetic addresses/alignment, zero-sized allocation storage, unwritten bytes, bounds, handle rejection, frees and trace. ninja_memory exercises lazy source handle publication, zero allocation and unavailable-method distinction; CD scan consumes the blocks.
accepted_judges.limits: Historical accepted paths only, not rerun. They prove the model contract at their cases, not actual Windows token/address choices, allocator reuse, reservation, host OOM or arbitrary constructor alignment. Caller oracles are not standalone HeapAlloc equivalence proofs.

src/loader/mpeg_timing.cpp.reason: Reference DirectShow metadata timing helper, with uncaptured splitter policy explicitly assumed by its sole runtime caller; excluded from actual native movie/import paths.
src/loader/mpeg_timing.cpp.semantic_justification: Complete header and implementation reviewed: local timing accumulator, 33-bit timestamp extraction, MPEG-1 pack/system/packet walk, E0 video filtering, stuffing/STD skips, PTS/PTS+DTS payload offsets, min/max timestamp aggregation, first in-packet sequence header size/rate decode and truncated integer conversion to 100 ns plus one frame. Format start codes, stream IDs, masks and rate fractions are numeric encodings, not addresses. Optional result means unsupported/malformed/missing stream metadata. There are no fixture-availability state members or recovered game branches. The duration formula is the reference HLE duration assumption, not recovered DirectShow splitter behavior. Actual use is AddSourceFilter in hle_dshow; it is neither native movie playback nor the importer despite the loader directory and generated asset-boundary label. Dense implementation still needs readability cleanup.

resolved_owners.resolution: MpegTiming is a result value and the parser has local state only plus immutable rate data. HleDshow Graph owns optional duration, run-start/position and completion queue. Its unknown duration before AddSourceFilter is graph lifecycle absence. Native MoviePlayer separately owns AVFoundation samples/timeline and audio presentation state.

resolved_consumers.resolution: Only maintained non-test direct parser caller is HLE AddSourceFilter: reads mapped host movie, stops on parser failure, stores duration and reports the uncaptured splitter assumption. stream_time/deliver_due/get_Duration consume that value, including EC_COMPLETE. Native app opens MoviePlayer on imported paths; completion uses decoder EOS, audio presentation frames and AVFoundation track end. Importer copies/hashes movie bytes and extracts clip/playlist declarations with separate Python PEImage; it never calls this C++ parser.

accepted_judges.accepted_scope: mpeg_timing unit builds a synthetic 640x480/code-4 stream with stuffing, STD, audio, PTS and PTS+DTS, verifies two video timestamps and 10 s plus one truncated frame; rejects MPEG-2 pack, broken length and absent PTS. Registered gate invocation additionally reads local RE-US.MPG.
accepted_judges.limits: Historical accepted path only, not rerun. This does not independently recover DirectShow duration/EC_COMPLETE policy or validate decoder/audio/hardware behavior. Marker validity, PTS wrap, split sequence headers, other rate codes and malformed tails are not established by this unit. ISO table comment is source attribution, not a spec verification performed here.

prioritized_findings.title: Reject relocation entries outside mapped image before dereferencing
prioritized_findings.description: rebased validates block size against the declared relocation directory extent, but not against mapped.size(). The entry loop unconditionally dereferences le(mapped,e,2). Static example: SizeOfImage 4096, relocation RVA 4088 and directory size 10, readable final 8-byte block header declaring block size 10. Both header reads succeed and block passes validation; first entry starts at byte 4096, le returns nullopt and operator* violates its precondition. parse accepts the directory metadata without checking mapped extent. This is an actual unchecked boundary in a malformed-image path, not an address-style violation or an observed supported-image failure.
prioritized_findings.suggested_followup: In a separate source/judge packet, bounds-check directory/block entries and retain explicit error results; add discriminating malformed-image coverage without weakening pinned-image checks.
